title: Trump Secretly Evacuated From Turkey Via Catering Truck After Iran Threat
excerpt: Israel warned the US of a specific Iranian plot to assassinate the president during the NATO summit in Ankara, prompting an elaborate deception involving a decoy Air Force One and a military jet.
body:
• Israel shared intelligence with the CIA alleging Iran had devised a new plot to assassinate Trump during the July NATO summit in Ankara, including a potential shoulder-fired missile threat to Air Force One.
  • Trump was secretly moved from Air Force One into a cleaned-out catering truck, driven 162 seconds across the tarmac to a C-32A military plane, while senior staff and journalists aboard Air Force One served as unwitting decoys.
  • Some US officials viewed the Israeli intelligence skeptically, questioning whether it was partly an effort to influence Trump's decision-making on military action against Iran.

President Donald Trump was secretly smuggled out of Turkey inside a catering truck during the NATO summit in Ankara on July 8, after Israeli intelligence warned of an Iranian assassination plot that included a possible shoulder-mounted missile strike on Air Force One, according to multiple US officials.

The elaborate ruse, first detailed by CNN on August 13, involved Trump boarding the presidential aircraft as expected, then quickly walking through to an exit on the opposite side where an emptied-out catering truck was waiting. He was driven 162 seconds across the tarmac to a smaller C-32A military plane that flew him to RAF Mildenhall in Britain, while Air Force One departed as a decoy with senior Cabinet members and journalists aboard.

The Intelligence and the Skepticism

Israel had shared intelligence with the CIA alleging Iran had developed a specific new plan to kill Trump. The Wall Street Journal first reported the warning, which came as the US-Iran conflict was at an inflection point. According to US officials, Iran had obtained detailed knowledge of Trump's hotel, his motorcade routes through the Turkish capital, and remained intent on killing him.

https://x.com/Nancy023922191/status/2087434146830504131

As the summit progressed, additional intelligence surfaced about a potential threat to Air Force One from a ground-launched missile near Ankara's airport. However, some within the CIA raised questions about the intelligence's credibility and whether Iran had the capability to carry out such an attack at a heavily fortified NATO summit.

"The threat was serious enough that extreme measures needed to be taken that day. We wouldn't have taken those steps otherwise."

— US official, speaking to CNN

Three US sources said American intelligence assessments before the trip showed no indication of a new, specific Iranian plot. Some officials believed the Israeli intelligence could be an effort to sway Trump toward intensifying military action against Iran.

The Catering Truck Escape

Gen. Dan Caine, the Joint Chiefs chairman, marshaled senior officials and the Secret Service inside the Beştepe Presidential Complex to devise the evacuation plan. The Secret Service determined the potential risk — however uncertain — was serious enough to warrant extreme measures.

To explain why he would not be flying home on the Qatar-donated Boeing 747 he had arrived on, Trump posted online that the plane would fly to a British airbase so troops could tour it. He said he would take the older Air Force One "for old time's sake." In reality, he would take neither.

Inside the catering container were Trump, executive assistant Natalie Harp, Oval Office operations director Walt Nauta, personnel office chief Dan Scavino, and Secret Service agents. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth also joined Trump on the C-32A. Left behind on Air Force One were Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, top policy adviser Stephen Miller, and other senior aides, many unaware the president was not aboard.

Aftermath and Lingering Questions

No militants were taken into custody and no evidence of a missile plot was recovered after Trump departed Turkey. Fighter jets were mustered to accompany both aircraft out of the country, suggesting officials believed both could face potential danger.

On August 12, Trump addressed the reports, insisting it was actually his plane — not the decoy — that was most at danger departing Turkey. He said: "Every major president faces many threats. I'm not concerned about anything."

"I'm on every single one of their lists. And so far, I guess I've been a little bit lucky, but that maybe doesn't last very long."

— President Donald Trump, speaking at the NATO summit in Ankara

The incident underscores the persistent threat Iran poses to Trump, who ordered the 2020 drone strike that killed Iranian General Qasem Soleimani. Multiple previous assassination plots linked to Iran have been prosecuted in US courts, including Asif Merchant's conviction in March 2026 and ongoing charges against Farhad Shakeri.

What This Means for the Diaspora

The revelation that Turkey, a nation bordering Iran and home to a significant diaspora population, was the site of such a dramatic security operation raises fresh questions about the safety environment in the region. For Indian Americans and other diaspora communities with business and family ties across the Middle East and Central Asia, the incident highlights the volatile security landscape in a region many traverse regularly.
